races.title: State Assembly, District 31
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Jim Polsgrove
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 31 in 2026. Fresno resident and retired civil servant with a 39-year engineering career at the Fresno Metropolitan Flood Control District, the City of Fresno and the County of Fresno. Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by the Republican Party of California, per Ballotpedia, which also lists several informal online voter-guide groups.

cands.gaps: We found no stated or documented position from Polsgrove on data centers, development or growth limits, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor purchases of homes and land, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His site speaks generally of lower taxes and less spending but gives no specifics on property taxes. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no news coverage or controversies about him. We did not find a record of any elected office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. His campaign biography is the only source for his career and roots, and we found no independent confirmation.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign biography says he was born in Fresno, spent his formative years on a ranch west of Fresno, and still lives in Fresno.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He worked 39 years in civil service in Fresno, retiring from the City of Fresno as a Supervising Engineering Technician after 31 years and then joining Fresno County as a Senior Engineering Technician / Utility Coordinator. His city work included managing right-of-way and special districts, the CPUC Rule 20A program, and capital improvement projects. He has not held elected office.
qual.why: He has long public-sector management and project experience, which is relevant to government work. He has no legislative service and no policy or budget-writing career, so the score is mid-range, not high.
qual.label: He has long public-sector management and project experience, which is relevant to government work. He has no legislative service and no policy or budget-writing career, so the score is mid-range, not high.

second-amendment.evidence: He says he will defend the right to keep and bear arms and will fight to eliminate gun laws he calls ineffective, replacing them with 'common sense' laws.

back-police-order.evidence: He says he will push new laws to hold criminals accountable, support first responders, and label organized looting as organized crime.

workers-first.evidence: He says he supports stricter consequences for people who cross the border illegally, along with stronger incentives for legal immigration and stronger border security.

cands.name: Annalisa Perea
cands.bio: Democrat and Fresno City Council member for District 1 since January 2023. Earlier served on the State Center Community College District board (Trustee Area 5, 2018–2022). Sister of former Fresno councilmember Henry Perea. Ran for California Assembly District 31 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, SEIU Local 521, IUOE Local 3 and Equality California are listed as endorsers for the 2026 Assembly race.
Speaker of the Assembly Robert Rivas endorsed her for Assembly District 31 (campaign press release, Feb 2026).
Attorney General Rob Bonta endorsed her for Assembly District 31 (campaign press release, Jan 2026).
California Professional Firefighters and CAL FIRE Local 2881 endorsed her (campaign press releases, Mar and May 2026).
California YIMBY and the Fresno Chamber of Commerce endorsed her (campaign press releases, Feb 2026 and Nov 2025).

cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace, where she grew up, when she came to California, or her education. We found no jobs outside elected office. We found no council or board votes, bills or official actions tied to data centers, property taxes, housing and land limits, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or schools. We found no stated positions on data centers or development, and no documented controversies or foreign ties. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, so her own stated priorities are limited to what her campaign site shows.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
